---
title: "check-fform-paren.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags `\name\paren{...}`
where an f form `\namef{...}` exists.
When a macro has an f form that takes its argument in braces,
write the f form rather than the macro followed by `\paren{`.
This is the companion check to
[ai-config#4597](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/ai-config/issues/4597);
it is [gha#1082](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1082).
Its rule alone failed at composition time in
[sds#261](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/sds/pull/261),
where `\fitproc\paren{...}` was typed by hand
although `\fitprocf` existed.

The check flags a macro name immediately followed by
`\paren{`, `\sb{`, `\cb{`, `\set{`, `\abs{`, `\norm{` or `\angb{`
on a line a pull request adds,
in `.qmd`, `.Rmd` and `.md` files,
when `\namef` is defined and wraps its argument in that same delimiter.
The delimiter is read from the f form's defining line,
following `\def` aliases;
an f form whose delimiter cannot be read is never suggested.
So `\log\abs{x}` passes when `\logf` builds in `\cb`.
Each finding reports the file, the line,
and the suggestion `\name\paren{...} -> \namef{...}`,
with the delimiter macro as written in place of `\paren`.
An alias of the operator counts as the operator:
`\Exp\sb{X}` is flagged when `\Expf` is defined.
The delimiter macros are the `DELIMITERS` constant in the script.

## Known f forms

The f forms are read from a macros file (`macros-file`,
default `latex-macros/macros.qmd`, the `latex-macros` submodule's file):
every `\providecommand{\XXXf}`, `\newcommand{\XXXf}` and `\def\XXXf` defines one.
When the file is missing, the check skips with a warning,
because without it no f form is known.
The reusable workflow checks out submodules by default
so the file is there.

The check does not flag:

- a delimiter macro with no macro directly before it;
- a macro with no f form (`\foo\paren{x}` when `\foof` is not defined);
- the f form itself (`\fitprocf{x}`);
- a macro and the delimiter macro separated by a space;
- a code fence or code span, an HTML comment, or YAML front matter;
- a line carrying, or following, `<!-- check-fform-paren: allow -->`.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing uses are not reflagged on every unrelated edit.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose,
for example to count the uses a repository still carries.

Every run prints how many lines, files and f forms it examined.

## Limitations

- A use split across lines (the macro at the end of one line,
  `\paren{` at the start of the next) is not found.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `macros-file`    | string  | `'latex-macros/macros.qmd'` | Path of the macros file whose `\providecommand{\XXXf}` and `\newcommand{\XXXf}` definitions name the known f forms. A missing file skips the check with a warning. |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.Rmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `submodules`     | string  | `'true'` | Passed to `actions/checkout`, so the `latex-macros` submodule is available. |
| `submodule-paths` | string  | `''`     | Whitespace-separated submodule paths to initialize instead of `submodules`, for a repository with a private submodule beside the public one this check needs. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `false` | Fail the workflow when a `\name\paren{...}` with an f form is found. Warn-only by default. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | `'ubuntu-latest'` | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-fform-paren.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags `\name\paren{...}` (or `\sb{`, `\cb{`) on lines a PR adds when a
# `\namef{...}` macro exists in the latex-macros submodule's macros.qmd.
# Warn-only by default. Skips with a warning when the macros file is missing.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check f forms written as name-paren

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-fform-paren.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   macros-file: 'latex-macros/macros.qmd'  # where the f forms are defined
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'    # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                              # block instead of warn (defaults to false)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-fform-paren.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-fform-paren.yml)
for the full caller stub.
